title: EdgeFlow: session-preserving active-active shift controller for hosted API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: Hosted API currently uses a simple region failover that drops streaming sessions or forces clients to reconnect when traffic is shifted across regions for capacity or maintenance. This causes visible user regressions for long-running streams and increases error budgets for high-latency customers. Goal: implement EdgeFlow, a controller that performs active-active traffic shifts at the gateway level while preserving session continuity and respecting SLOs. EdgeFlow will coordinate graded traffic bleed, token-preserving stream handoff, and circuit-breaker engagement to avoid tail-latency amplification and cascading failures. It must be compatible with existing routing policy rules, KV prefix cache semantics, and streaming protocol (HTTP/2 + chunked / websockets), and integrate with Console telemetry and rollback mechanisms.
acceptance_criteria: Can shift up to 80% of steady-state TCP streaming sessions from region A to region B within 90s with <1% stream reconnections observed in Canary test using synthetic workload
During a forced shift due to regional capacity pressure, system engages circuit-breakers and sheds low-priority burst load before impacting P99 latency on production routes
Session token handoff preserves incremental KV-cache lookups and allows resumed stream continuation without model state loss for gated streaming APIs
Redwood Console shows per-route SLO impact, pre/post-shift token preservation rate, and automatic rollback trigger if error budget burn exceeds 5% within a 10 minute window
Comprehensive runbook and automated canary (k8s job + synthetic client harness) exist and are documented in Confluence with post-mortem template
